facts.fact_text: On 24 November 2007 a group of opposition politicians organised protest rallies in several Russian cities, including Moscow.
On 24 November 2007 the applicants attended a gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt.

According to the applicants, at 3 p.m. on 24 November 2007, at the end of the gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt, the applicants started walking to the location of another authorised gathering on Chistoprudnyy Boulevard.
The Government alleged that some 1,500 people took part in the procession on 24 November 2007.
The applicants' route on 24 November 2007 was blocked by the riot police.
The applicants were arrested on 24 November 2007.
On 24 November 2007 the Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow found the first applicant guilty of both charges.
The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow sentenced the first applicant to five days' administrative detention.
The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow found the second applicant guilty of both charges.
The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow sentenced the second applicant to five days' administrative detention.
The applicants served their sentences in detention centres for administrative offenders (спецприемник).
The other applicants (third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh applicants) were convicted of administrative offences.
The first applicant was charged with breaching the established procedure for conducting public events, an offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The first applicant was charged with disobeying lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant was charged with breaching the established procedure for conducting public events, an offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant was charged with disobeying lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The administrative detention of the first and second applicants was ordered with reference to Article 27.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
A summary of the relevant domestic law is contained in Kasparov and Others v. Russia (no. 21613/07, § 35, 3 October 2013).
A summary of the relevant domestic law is contained in Navalnyy and Yashin v. Russia (no. 76204/11, §§ 43-44, 4 December 2014).
Police officer M. stated that after the public gathering on 24 November 2007 the first applicant had participated in an unauthorised march down Myasnitskaya Street towards Chistoprudnyy Boulevard.
Police officer U. stated that after the public gathering on 24 November 2007 the first applicant had participated in an unauthorised march down Myasnitskaya Street towards Chistoprudnyy Boulevard.

The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow established that the first applicant had marched among some 1,500 people in what had constituted an unauthorised public event on 24 November 2007.
The gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt on 24 November 2007 had been approved by the authorities.

According to the applicants, at 3 p.m. on 24 November 2007, at the end of the gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt, the applicants started walking to the location of another authorised gathering on Chistoprudnyy Boulevard.
The authorised gathering on Chistoprudnyy Boulevard took place between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. on 24 November 2007.
The first applicant testified that he had been arrested while walking alongside other people from one authorised gathering to another on 24 November 2007.
The first applicant testified that when he had seen that the path had been blocked by the police he had turned back as ordered, but as he had walked away he had been arrested.
The first applicant insisted that there had been no other way of complying with the police's order to disperse than to turn back.
The first applicant denied that there had been an organised march on 24 November 2007.

The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow established that the first applicant had marched among some 1,500 people in what had constituted an unauthorised public event on 24 November 2007.

The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow dismissed the first applicant's testimony as false, finding that it contradicted the police officers' testimony and reports.
The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow found police officers M. and U.'s testimony and reports trustworthy because they had "no vested interest".
